title: MPP failure: a used credential is sent again (replay)
summary: A credential that already paid is presented a second time, by the same client or by an attacker who copied it. The id is single use, so the server answers 402 with invalid-challenge and settles nothing.

steps.label: 402 with challenge
steps.detail: Server issues a bound challenge with expires.

steps.label: First retry pays
steps.detail: The first credential is verified and settled; the server marks the id as consumed and returns 200 with a receipt.

steps.label: Same credential again
steps.detail: A second request carries the identical credential. Credentials are bearer tokens, so a leaked one looks exactly like this.

steps.label: Look up the id
steps.detail: The id is already consumed. The method proof is single use too, so even a stateless server would fail the on-chain check.

steps.label: 402, fresh challenge, invalid-challenge
steps.detail: The server answers with a new challenge and an invalid-challenge problem. Concurrent duplicates must yield at most one settlement, so servers use atomic operations or locks on the id.

payload.content:
HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required
Cache-Control: no-store
Content-Type: application/problem+json
WWW-Authenticate: Payment id="pT7yHnKmQ2wErXsZ5vCbNl", realm="api.example.com", method="tempo", intent="charge", expires="2026-10-11T12:20:00Z", request="eyJ..."

{"type":"https://paymentauth.org/problems/invalid-challenge","title":"Invalid challenge","status":402}

# Illustrative example, spec version draft-httpauth-payment-01

failures.condition: The server runs mppx 0.13.5 or later and the replayed credential is a Tempo charge (SDK behavior, not draft text)
failures.outcome: 403 with problem type verification-failed and no new challenge, so the client does not pay again.
